deep.reconstruction:
Context: Gauss's note 'Begründung des Planum' (previous page). Definition 1: the plane P through A perpendicular to a line AB is the union of all lines AD with angle DAB = 90°, i.e. the surface swept when AD rotates about AB. Article 3 shows by congruence ('Deckung') that if AD = AD' lie in P, then every point T of the line DD' lies in P. Article 4, Theorem: if T and V lie in P, the whole line TV lies in P. Case I: A lies on TV (immediate from the definition). Case II: AT = AV (this is art. 3). Case III: AT > AV.

This page finishes Case III. Notation shifts here: the interior point is now called U, and V (or W) is a point on the arc. Take the circle in P with centre A and radius r = AT. Let K be the point with AK = AT on TA produced, so KT is a diameter. U lies in the closed disc (AU < r), in one of the half-discs cut off by KT. A segment TW moves with one end fixed at T and the other end W running along the semicircular arc from K to T. Each position TW is a chord with AT = AW, so by Case II it lies entirely in P. The moving chord sweeps the half-disc and has exhausted it when W reaches T. Hence in some position, call it TV, the chord passes through U. The segment TU is part of the line TV, which lies in P, so TU lies in P.

Supplementary claim, proved by contradiction: the motion fills the whole half-disc. Suppose a part is never reached and U lies in it. Take a sphere (centre T, implicitly) with radius rho < TU. It divides the half-disc into M (outside the sphere) and M' (inside). Then U is in M, since TU > rho. Let W be the point where the sphere cuts the arc. Every point of chord TW is at distance at most TW = rho from T, so TW lies within M'. Therefore M, and with it U, lies in the figure K-T-W bounded by TK, TW and the arc WK. That figure is described while the moving line turns from TK to TW. So U is reached, contradicting the assumption.

Modern version: for U in the half-disc, the ray from T through U meets the circle again at a unique point W(U) on the arc, and U lies on the segment TW. So U belongs to a chord TW, which lies in P by Case II.
errors: Notation inconsistency with the previous page: the point to be reached is called V there (with the arc called KVW). Here it becomes U, and V/W name points on the arc ('Lage TV', 'die gerade TU ist ... Theil der geraden TV').

The 'vollkommne Strenge' completeness argument is essentially circular. It assumes that the subregion K-T-W is swept as the line turns from TK to TW, which is the very kind of claim being proved. Real rigor needs a continuity or intermediate-value argument, or the direct observation that the line TU meets the arc at a point W with U between T and W.
The centre of the auxiliary sphere (T) is not stated explicitly. 'so dass A ausserhalb' must mean 'M ausserhalb', since A is the centre of the circle, not a region.
Edge case not discussed: U on the diameter KT, i.e. the line through A. This is covered by Case I, so the omission is harmless.

results.what: Proof that a line through two points of the 'plane' (defined as the surface of revolution generated by a line rotating perpendicularly about an axis) lies entirely in it. Reduced via the sweeping chords of a half-disc to the isosceles case.
results.modern_name: Foundations of geometry: the line–plane incidence axiom derived from the rotation definition of the plane
results.usually_credited_to: Rotation/perpendicular definitions of the plane are old (Euclid commentators, Leibniz, 18th-c. elementary texts). Deriving Euclid's plane axiom from it was discussed by Gauss, Bolyai, Lobachevsky, Crelle and later Hilbert-era axiomatics.

results.what: Argument that the chords TW, as W runs over the semicircle, fill the half-disc
results.modern_name: Elementary continuity / star-shapedness of the disc with respect to a boundary point

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's interest in the foundations of geometry, including the definition of the plane, is well documented. Similar notes on the 'Planum' appear in Werke VIII. The argument is elementary and not fully rigorous, so it adds no new mathematical result.

checkable.sympy: b,x,y=symbols('b x y',real=True); B=Matrix([0,0,b]); C=Matrix([0,0,-b]); T=Matrix([x,y,0]); simplify((T-B).dot(T-B)-(T-C).dot(T-C))==0
checkable.asserts: Any point T of the plane z=0 is equidistant from B and C symmetric about A, the key congruence used in art. 3.

checkable.sympy: r,t=symbols('r t',positive=True); u1,u2=symbols('u1 u2',real=True); T=Matrix([r,0]); U=Matrix([u1,u2]); W=T+t*(U-T); sol=solve(W.dot(W)-r**2,t); sol
checkable.asserts: The line from T through U meets the circle of radius r again at parameter t = 2r(r-u1)/((u1-r)^2+u2^2). This is at least 1 when u1^2+u2^2 <= r^2, so U lies on the chord TW.

checkable.sympy: r,s,phi=symbols('r s phi',positive=True); W=Matrix([r*cos(phi),r*sin(phi)]); T=Matrix([r,0]); P=T+s*(W-T); simplify(P.dot(P)-r**2 - (s**2-s)*(W-T).dot(W-T))==0
checkable.asserts: For 0<=s<=1, |P|^2 - r^2 = (s^2-s)|W-T|^2 <= 0, so each chord TW lies in the disc.

transcription_corrections: 'es sei dies die Lage TV' / 'durch V gegangen': in the image the point passed through is likely U ('durch U gegangen'), consistent with 'Die gerade TU ist also nur ein Theil der geraden TV'.
'so dass A ausserhalb' should read 'so dass M ausserhalb' (the region M lies outside the sphere).
'der Figur KTWK[?]' is the figure K T W (bounded by TK, TW and the arc WK); the first letter is overwritten (K over another letter).
The trailing '4' at the bottom is a later folio/page number in pencil, not part of the text.
